    end
    subgraph process["WordPress PHP process (trusted code)"]
        cfg["wp-config.php constants, env vars, add-on sources, sc_wpun_config_value"]
        addon["Add-on modules and hook callbacks"]
        handlers["admin-post handlers and options.php save"]
        checker["Update_Checker (cron or on demand)"]
        renderer["Notification_Renderer: HTML, plain text, Markdown"]
        dispatcher["Dispatcher and channel modules"]
        db[("Options: sc_wpun_settings, sc_wpun_channels, sc_wpun_state")]
    end
    mail["Mail (wp_mail)"]

    anon -- "admin-post.php, options.php" --> handlers
    browser -- "POST + security token" --> handlers
    handlers --> db
    hdr -- "get_plugins(), wp_get_themes()" --> checker
    wporg -- "update_* site transients" --> checker
    db --> checker
    cfg --> checker
    checker --> renderer --> dispatcher
    addon --> dispatcher
    dispatcher -- "wp_mail()" --> mail
    dispatcher -- "wp_safe_remote_*" --> svc
    svc -- "status, Retry-After" --> dispatcher
    dispatcher --> db
    db -- "settings screen, Site Health" --> browser

The trust boundaries are:

  • the HTTP request into admin-post.php and options.php;
  • third-party data read from headers and transients;
  • outbound requests and the responses that come back;
  • the settings screen, where stored data is rendered.

docs.title: Assets
docs.text: Asset Where it lives Why it matters Channel secrets (webhook URLs, tokens) sc_wpun_channels, or constants and env vars They let someone post into the site owner's chat or services. Recipient lists, From and Reply-To sc_wpun_channels Changing them redirects or spoofs the site's mail. Settings and schedule sc_wpun_settings, cron event sc_wpun_update_check Silencing them hides the updates a site needs. Delivery state sc_wpun_state It holds what was already notified, last_result, retry_at and last_reminder. The site's update inventory Sent in notifications It shows which outdated, possibly vulnerable, plugins a site runs. The release zip GitHub release, WordPress.org SVN A tampered build reaches every site that updates.

docs.title: 1. admin-post handlers
docs.text:
All are registered in Plugin::register_admin_hooks() (includes/class-plugin.php), except the Slack notice dismiss, which Plugin registers next to the notice. There are no admin_post_nopriv_*, wp_ajax_* or REST routes.

Action Handler Token action Method sc_wpun_send_test Channels_Tab::handle_test_send sc_wpun_send_test_<id> POST sc_wpun_channel_toggle Channels_Tab::handle_toggle sc_wpun_channel_toggle_<id> POST sc_wpun_channel_duplicate Channels_Tab::handle_duplicate sc_wpun_channel_duplicate_<id> POST sc_wpun_channel_delete Channels_Tab::handle_delete sc_wpun_channel_delete_<id> POST sc_wpun_check_now Check_Now::handle sc_wpun_check_now POST sc_wpun_save_channel Channel_Form::handle_save sc_wpun_save_channel_<new\|edit>_<type\|id> POST sc_wpun_dismiss_slack_notice Slack_Notice::handle_dismiss sc_wpun_dismiss_slack_notice GET (link)

Trust boundary: any HTTP client can reach admin-post.php. Unauthenticated requests fire only admin_post_nopriv_*, and the plugin registers none. The Semgrep rule wpun-no-nopriv-hooks (make sast, #216) fails the build if one is added.

STRIDE Threat Control Proof E A user without the capability changes channels, sends messages or runs the check. Each handler checks current_user_can( Settings_Page::capability() ) first, and refuses with a 403 and no change. test-channels-tab.php (test_nonce_and_capability_are_enforced_for_every_action), test-channel-form.php (test_nonce_and_capability_are_required, test_refusals_change_nothing, test_the_handler_answers_403_when_refused), test-check-now.php (test_a_refused_request_runs_nothing), test-test-send.php, test-slack-notice.php. security/test-capability-matrix.php (#220): discovers every admin_post_*/wp_ajax_* hook the plugin registers, fails on one without a request builder, and sends each one ten refused requests: logged out, subscriber, editor, administrator without manage_options, and administrator with no, empty, other-action, other-channel or other-user token, or the fields in the wrong method. Each must die with 403 and change nothing (options, user meta, mail, HTTP), with a positive control. The unauthenticated ZAP pass (make dast, #222). S/T CSRF: another site makes an administrator's browser post the action. A security token per action. Row actions and the form bind it to the channel id (and the mode and type), so a token for one channel can't act on another. The tests above. security/test-capability-matrix.php (#220) covers the wrong-action, other-channel and other-user tokens for every hook. T Tampered id, mode or type reaches the store. sanitize_key( wp_unslash() ) and is_string checks. Unknown ids and types are refused, and code-defined and externally set instances have no row actions. test-channels-tab.php, test-channel-form.php. T Open redirect after the action. Redirects use wp_safe_redirect() to the settings page. WPCS WordPress.Security.SafeRedirect (make lint). #222 checks the redirect targets. R An administrator denies changing a channel. Not addressed. WordPress has no audit log, and the plugin doesn't add one. Accepted for 2.0.0. n/a D Repeated Check now or test sends flood a mail service. Capability and security token limit this to administrators, who are trusted. As above.

The dismiss link is a GET that changes state, but only the current user's own meta (sc_wpun_dismissed_slack_notice). It still needs the security token and the capability.

docs.title: 2. The settings screen
docs.text:
The General tab saves through core's options.php (register_setting with sc_wpun_settings_validate, and option_page_capability_sc_wpun_settings returns the same capability). The Channels tab and the channel form use the handlers above. Field types are in includes/class-field-types.php, class-boolean-field.php and class-enum-field.php. They render through includes/admin/class-field-renderer.php.

Trust boundary: administrator input in, and stored, external and add-on data rendered back out.

STRIDE Threat Control Proof E Someone without the capability opens the page. Settings_Page::settings_page() refuses with a 403. Core's options.php checks the filtered capability. test-settings-screen.php (test_the_page_refuses_users_without_the_capability). T Invalid or hostile values are stored. Each field type sanitises and validates. Text uses sanitize_text_field. URLs need an http or https scheme and pass esc_url_raw. Email lists go through sanitize_email and is_email. Numbers are bounded, enums are allowlisted, and only declared fields are kept. Unknown notify keys and frequencies are refused. test-field-types.php, test-settings-validation.php, test-boolean-field.php, test-enum-field.php, test-field-showcase.php. security/test-settings-input.php (#220): hostile payloads through every field type, for the email schema and an add-on schema, and javascript:, data: and file: URLs. ZAP fuzzes the field showcase (make dast, #222). I Stored XSS through a field value, an error message or a channel's last result. Late escaping (esc_html, esc_attr, esc_url) in the renderer and tabs, checked by WPCS's WordPress.Security.EscapeOutput. Psalm follows options and transients to echo. test-settings-markup.php, test-channel-form.php (test_an_error_without_a_field_is_plain_text), make lint, make taint (#218). security/test-stored-xss.php (#220): payloads in every tab and form, the reflected tab, action, id and type parameters, and the channel list with its last result. I A secret is shown on the page. Secret fields are never rendered: the renderer only learns whether a value is saved ('1'/''). An empty input keeps the stored value, and <name>__clear removes it. secret => true works on any type. Values set in code show as read-only and are never echoed unless the schema opts in with show_external, which email uses for its non-secret fields only. test-field-types.php (test_render_secret_never_outputs_value, test_secret_keep_and_clear, test_secret_flag_on_other_types), test-channel-form.php (test_secrets_are_never_output_and_can_be_kept_or_cleared, test_secrets_are_not_kept_for_the_error_round_trip), test-channels-tab.php (test_duplicate_does_not_store_external_secrets). security/test-secrets.php (#220): a secret set through the form, a constant and an env var never shows, apart from the placeholder or its source. E An add-on schema renders unescaped markup. Add-on code is trusted (see Scope). Its custom render callbacks are its own responsibility. docs/developers/writing-a-module.md.

docs.title: 3. Update data
docs.text:
Plugin and theme names, versions, authors and URLs come from third-party headers (get_plugins(), wp_get_themes()) and from api.wordpress.org through the update_core, update_plugins and update_themes site transients (includes/class-update-checker.php). They become Notification_Item values and are rendered as HTML email, plain text or Markdown (includes/class-notification-renderer.php), as well as in the update nag and Site Health.

Trust boundary: third-party strings in, and markup out.

STRIDE Threat Control Proof T/I A plugin name such as <script>… or "><img onerror=…> runs in HTML mail or an admin page. Notification_Item collapses control characters so each value is a single line. The HTML renderer escapes every value with esc_html or esc_url. Markdown escapes its special characters and links only explicit http(s) URLs. Plain text is not HTML, and it is sent as text/plain. test-notification.php (test_html_escapes_values, test_markdown_escapes_special_characters, test_markdown_drops_unsafe_link_targets, test_plain_text_is_not_escaped), test-message-snapshot.php, make taint (sources get_plugins, get_plugin_data, wp_get_themes, get_site_transient). security/test-stored-xss.php (#220): the payloads through a mocked update check into the HTML and plain-text mail (no live markup, no double encoding), the nag, the channel list, Site Health and every tab. T A javascript: link in a header reaches a notification. esc_url in HTML, and the http(s)-only rule in Markdown. test-notification.php. security/test-stored-xss.php (#220). D Huge or many items blow a channel's size limit. Renderer limits truncate and summarise. test-renderer-limits.php. I The update inventory leaks to someone who shouldn't see it. It goes only to recipients and channels an administrator set up. The hide_updates setting removes the nag for users who can't update_core. test-update-nag.php, test-routing.php.

Two things the security tests found are out of scope or accepted:

  • WordPress core's own update nag prints the update_core version without escaping. That is core's output, not the plugin's, and the plugin adds nothing to the nag.
  • A right-to-left override (U+202E) in a plugin name survives into the mail and the admin. It can make a name display misleadingly, but it can't inject markup. Accepted.

docs.title: 4. Configuration sources
docs.text:
Any setting or channel field can come from a wp-config.php constant (SC_WPUN_SETTING_<NAME>, SC_WPUN_CHANNEL_<ID>__<FIELD>) or from an environment variable. Environment variables are off unless SC_WPUN_LOAD_FROM_ENV or the sc_wpun_load_from_env filter turns them on. Add-ons can register sources with sc_wpun_config_sources, and the sc_wpun_config_value filter has the last word (includes/class-config.php).

Trust boundary: none to the outside. All of these are server-side and trusted. The risks are values that are malformed or leak.

STRIDE Threat Control Proof T A malformed value breaks a channel or bypasses validation. Every value is cast to the field's type and validated like form input. A rejected value is not used anywhere and is listed, without the value, in Site Health. A throwing or junk source is skipped. test-config.php (test_precedence_for_a_setting, test_a_throwing_source_is_skipped, test_a_junk_source_is_dropped), test-config-channels.php (test_a_rejected_value_is_not_used_anywhere). I A secret from wp-config or the environment shows up in a page, a log, Site Health or debug output. Config_Value hides secret values in debug output and string casts. Channel_Instance::__debugInfo redacts. Reports name only the source, never the value. External values are read-only on the form. test-config-channels.php (test_a_secret_never_leaks, test_a_valid_secret_is_used_and_not_logged), test-config.php (test_external_settings_render_read_only). security/test-secrets.php (#220): Site Health debug data, _doing_it_wrong messages, notices, the debug log and print_r/var_dump of an instance. E An add-on uses the source API to override another plugin's values. Add-ons are trusted (see Scope). The order of precedence is documented and fixed. docs/developers/configuration-sources.md.

docs.title: 5. Outbound requests
docs.text:
Email is the only built-in channel, and it sends with wp_mail(). HTTP channels come from add-ons. The example add-on (examples/wpun-example-channel/) shows the expected pattern: wp_safe_remote_post(), a timeout, and Delivery_Result failures that leave out the address. Retry-After from a response is parsed by Delivery_Result::retry_after_from_response(). It is capped at 7 days (State::MAX_RETRY_AFTER), and it defers only that instance.

STRIDE Threat Control Proof I/E SSRF: a channel URL points at 127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254 or the LAN. wp_safe_remote_* refuses private and loopback hosts unless the site allows them with core's http_request_host_is_external filter. URL fields accept only http(s). The Semgrep rule wpun-outbound-http-safe-only refuses wp_remote_* and other HTTP clients in the plugin and the example. Psalm treats wp_safe_remote_* URLs as SSRF sinks. make sast (#216), make taint (one baselined, reviewed finding in the example add-on), test-example-channel.php. security/test-outbound-requests.php (#220): every request of the example add-on carries reject_unsafe_urls. Loopback, link-local (metadata), private and IPv6 loopback addresses are refused, and only a host the site allows passes. The email module makes no HTTP request. D A service answers Retry-After: 99999999 or garbage and silences the channel for good. The header is parsed strictly, the wait is capped at a week, and the cap is per instance. test-retry-after.php. I An error message or last_result leaks the webhook URL. The example's failures leave out the address, and the module guide tells add-ons never to put a secret in a result, notice or log, nor to pass on the HTTP API's error messages as they are. test-example-channel.php (test_a_wp_error_is_a_failure_without_the_address). security/test-secrets.php (#220) checks last_result and the delivery state. T Mail header injection through the From name, the subject, the recipients or the payload filters. Recipients and header lines with CR or LF are dropped after the payload filters (Email_Channel::checked_payload). The subject is built from sanitize_text_field values, and PHPMailer encodes it. From and Reply-To are validated email settings. test-hooks.php (header lines with line breaks are dropped), test-email-channel.php. #228 re-checks this by hand.

docs.title: 6. Public hook and add-on API
docs.text:
Add-ons register channel modules, item types and config sources, and they hook the documented actions and filters (docs/developers/hooks.md). Modules declare the API version they need, and a module that needs a newer one is refused, with a notice for administrators.

What an add-on is trusted to do: run any PHP, read and send its own channel's settings, change payloads through the filters, and supply config values. What the plugin still guarantees when an add-on is used as documented:

  • a module's secrets are never rendered or logged by the plugin;
  • schema values are sanitised and validated before the module sees them;
  • an exception in one module becomes a failed Delivery_Result and doesn't stop the other channels;
  • payload filters can't inject mail headers (see 5);
  • the capability for the screens comes from one filter, sc_wpun_capability, and a non-string or empty value falls back to manage_options.

Proof: test-extension-api.php, test-dispatcher.php, test-channel-api-constraint.php, test-api-version.php, test-contract.php, make check-public-api (modules use only the public API), and make check-hooks (every hook is documented).

docs.title: 7. Cron and on-demand runs
docs.text:
sc_wpun_update_check (WP-Cron) and sc_wpun_run_check (on demand, for example from WP-CLI) both run Update_Checker. Check now (1) calls the same code after its capability and security token checks.

STRIDE Threat Control Proof D/T Overlapping runs, such as cron and Check now together, deliver the same update twice. Accepted trade-off: there is no lock. A duplicate message is harmless, and a lock adds failure modes, such as a stale lock that silences notifications. n/a (recorded decision) E Anyone triggers a run. Visitors can only trigger WP-Cron at its schedule, never on demand. sc_wpun_run_check is an action for trusted code only. test-run-check.php, test-scheduling.php, test-check-now.php.

docs.title: 8. Stored data
docs.text:
These options are stored per site: sc_wpun_settings, sc_wpun_settings_ver, sc_wpun_channels and sc_wpun_state. There is also user meta for notices and form round trips. Secrets are stored in plain text in the options table, like every WordPress plugin's. Anyone who can read the database or run code can read them. A site that wants them out of the database sets them in wp-config.php constants or environment variables (4).

STRIDE Threat Control Proof I Secrets leak through var_dump, print_r or debug plugins. Channel_Instance::__debugInfo and Config_Value redact. test-notification.php, test-config-channels.php. I Data is left behind after uninstall. uninstall.php deletes every option, transient, user meta key and cron event, on every site of a network. test-uninstall.php, make test-dist (install, activate, deactivate, uninstall). T Options changed directly or by another plugin hold invalid data. Values are checked again when read: the store skips invalid instances and missing settings get their defaults. test-channel-store.php (test_invalid_entries_are_skipped_on_read), test-settings-state.php (test_missing_settings_get_defaults).

docs.title: 9. Build and release
docs.text:
The release zip is built by bin/build-dist.sh from the files .distignore doesn't exclude, and the build is reproducible. release-please opens the release PR with a GitHub App token and, when it is merged, makes a draft release with no tag. The release job then runs in the release environment, which is limited to main and needs the maintainer's approval. It builds the zip and its SBOM, attests the zip's provenance and SBOM, creates a signed annotated tag at the release commit, uploads the assets and publishes the release. The WordPress.org deploy (#57, not built yet) will run on the published release in the wordpress-org environment, which needs a reviewer.

STRIDE Threat Control Proof T A malicious or compromised workflow, action or tool image. Actions and tool images are pinned by digest. Workflows default to permissions: {} or read-only, and credentials aren't persisted. CODEOWNERS covers .github/ and bin/. Dependabot waits 14 days before proposing a new release. make check-workflows (actionlint, zizmor, #210), OpenSSF Scorecard (#224). T A vulnerable dependency. Runtime code has no dependencies (make dist-check enforces it). Development dependencies are audited. make audit (composer audit, OSV-Scanner), dependency review on PRs, make audit-images (Trivy), all #214. I A committed secret. Secrets live outside the repo. gitleaks scans the history, the tree and the zip. make secrets (gitleaks, #212). T Unreviewed changes on main. Branch protection: PRs, signed commits, linear history and the required checks. Scorecard Branch-Protection (#224). The accepted gaps are in SECURITY.md. S/T A tampered zip on GitHub. The zip is reproducible from the tag. The release job attests its build provenance and its SBOM, and checks the attestation before it publishes. make dist-repro on every PR, gh attestation verify in the release job (#226). S/T A forged or moved release tag. Tags are annotated and signed with a dedicated SSH key, held in the release environment. The v* ruleset forbids updating or deleting them. A re-run reuses the tag only if it points at the release commit and its signature checks out against .github/release-signers. make test-release (bin/sign-release-tag.sh), the release tags ruleset (#224, #226). S/T A tampered zip on WordPress.org. Not yet. Planned: the deploy runs only after the attestation of the zip it deploys checks out. #57.

User guide
docs.text:
WP Updates Notifier checks your site on a schedule and tells you when WordPress, a plugin or a theme has an update waiting. This guide is for the people who install and look after the site.

  • Getting started: what you need, installing the plugin, the email channel it sets up, sending a test and running a check.
  • Settings: how often to check, what to be told about, and what the Status line says.
  • Channels: where notifications go. Add, edit, switch off, duplicate and delete channels, send each kind of update to the right one, and the email options.
  • How notifications work: why you hear about each update once, what happens when a send fails, and what a message contains.
  • Settings in code: setting options and channels from wp-config.php or environment variables.
  • Troubleshooting: no emails, old data, a system cron, deliverability, a wrong address in a message and more.

If you write code, the developer guide covers extending the plugin.

docs.title: Channels
docs.text:
A channel is a place where notifications are sent. WP Updates Notifier comes with one kind, Email. You can have as many channels as you like, for example one that sends everything to you and another that sends only WordPress updates to a client.

Open them on the Channels tab of Settings → Updates Notifier. The table shows, for each channel:

  • Label: the name you gave it, with the actions underneath. A channel set up in code also says Defined in code.
  • Module: the kind of channel, such as Email.
  • Enabled: On or Off.
  • Routing: what the channel receives. All updates means no limit.
  • Last delivery: Never, Sent with the date and time, or Failed with the date and time and the reason.

A test message does not count as a delivery, so it never changes Last delivery.

docs.title: Add a channel
docs.text:
1. Click Add channel.
  2. Choose a module from the list. On a standard install that is Email.
  3. Give it a Label. The channel's id is made from the label when you save it and cannot be changed afterwards.
  4. Fill in the settings (see the email options) and choose its routing.
  5. Click Add channel.

On the form, Enabled is Send notifications through this channel. Untick it to save the channel without using it yet.

docs.title: Updates that are already waiting
docs.text:
A new channel has been told about nothing, so its first check sends it everything that is waiting for an update, even if other channels were told about those updates long ago.

If you only want updates that appear from now on, tick Don't send the updates that are already waiting. This box appears when you add a channel or edit one that is switched off, and it applies when you save the channel switched on.

docs.title: Edit a channel
docs.text: Click Edit under the channel's label, change what you need and click Save channel.

docs.title: Send a test message
docs.text:
Click Send test under a channel. A notice at the top says whether it was sent, and if it failed, why. The channel must be switched on.

A test goes only to that channel and is not cut down by its routing.

docs.title: Switch a channel off or on
docs.text:
Click Disable under the channel. Nothing is sent through a switched-off channel, and nothing is recorded as sent, so when you click Enable again it receives everything that is waiting. To avoid that, edit the channel while it is off and tick Don't send the updates that are already waiting before you switch it on.

If a constant or environment variable sets whether the channel is enabled, the channel shows "Set by" and the source, and there is no Disable or Enable action. See Settings in code.

docs.title: Duplicate a channel
docs.text: Click Duplicate to copy a channel's settings and routing, for example to send the same options to another address. The copy is called "label (copy)" and is switched off. Edit it, change what you need and tick Enabled when it is ready.

docs.title: Delete a channel
docs.text: Click Delete and confirm. The channel's settings and delivery history are removed, and this cannot be undone. If you add a channel again later it starts with no history.

docs.title: Channels defined in code
docs.text: A channel defined in code is read-only. It shows Defined in code and only offers Send test. See Settings in code.

docs.title: Choose what each channel receives
docs.text:
Each channel has a Routing section. Use it to send some kinds of update to some channels only.

  • Item types: tick WordPress, Plugins or Themes to receive only those. Tick nothing to receive every type, including any that an add-on adds later.
  • Plugins and themes: All, or Only active ones.
  • WordPress updates: All, or Only major releases.
  • Reminders: Never (the default), Daily or Weekly. See Reminders.

Routing works on top of the General settings. Those decide what the plugin looks at, and routing then narrows what each channel gets. If Notify about plugin updates? is No, no channel can receive plugin updates. If it is Yes, but only active plugins, choosing All here still gives you only the active ones. The form adds a note under an option when a General setting limits it.

docs.title: Reminders
docs.text:
By default a channel is told about each update once. Set Reminders to Daily or Weekly to be reminded about updates you have not installed yet.

  • A reminder is one message that lists every update still waiting for that channel. It is marked as a reminder: the email subject is "WP Updates Notifier: reminder of updates waiting for" followed by your site name, and the first line says "Reminder: these updates are still waiting for" followed by your site name and its address.
  • A new update is still sent at once, as usual. If a new update turns up in the same check as a reminder that is due, you get one message, the reminder, with the new update in it.
  • The first reminder comes one interval after an update starts waiting for the channel. Reminders stop when nothing is waiting any more.
  • Each channel has its own setting, so you can, for example, remind only one address each week.
  • The Routing column shows it, for example "Reminders: Weekly".

Reminders are worked out at each check, so they can not come more often than your frequency to check. See How notifications work.

docs.title: The email options
docs.text:
Option What it does Send to Required. One or more email addresses, separated by commas. From address The address the email comes from. Leave it empty to use the WordPress default. Only set an address at a domain this site is allowed to send mail for. If you set it, the sender name is "WP Updates Notifier". Reply-To address Where replies go. Optional. Format Plain text (the default) or HTML. Subject prefix Text put before the subject, followed by a space. Optional.

The subject is "WP Updates Notifier: updates available for" followed by your site name. With the prefix [Client] it becomes "[Client] WP Updates Notifier: updates available for My Site".

Why the From address matters is covered under Why does the email not arrive?.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• WordPress 6.7 or newer.
  • PHP 7.4 or newer.
  • A single WordPress site. WP Updates Notifier 2.0.0 does not support multisite networks.

docs.title: Install
docs.text: Search for "WP Updates Notifier" under Plugins → Add New and click Install Now, then Activate. The home page lists the other ways to install it.

docs.title: What you get straight away
docs.text:
On a new install the plugin sets up:

  • A check that runs every hour (Once Hourly).
  • One channel called Email. It is switched on and sends to the email address in Settings → General (the site's administration email address).
  • Notifications about WordPress, plugin and theme updates, all of them.

Because the check is due as soon as you activate the plugin, the first one runs on one of the next page loads of your site. If updates are waiting, you get an email about them.

docs.title: Open the settings
docs.text:
Go to Settings → Updates Notifier. There are two tabs:

  • General: the Status line, the Check for updates and notify now button, and the settings. See Settings.
  • Channels: where notifications are sent. See Channels.

By default you need the manage_options capability to see them, which administrators have.

docs.title: Send a test message
docs.text:
Check that the email arrives before you rely on it.

  1. Open the Channels tab.
  2. Find Email in the table and click Send test.
  3. A notice says Test message sent through Email. The subject of the email is "WP Updates Notifier: test message for" followed by your site name.

The notice means WordPress handed the message to your mail system. It does not prove the message was delivered. If it does not arrive, see Why does the email not arrive?.

The channel must be switched on to send a test.

docs.title: Change where emails go
docs.text: Click Edit under Email and change Send to. Separate several addresses with commas. The other options are in Channels.

docs.title: Run a check now
docs.text:
On the General tab, click Check for updates and notify now. The plugin runs the same check as the schedule and tells you what happened:

  • Checked just now. Nothing new to send.
  • Checked just now. Sent to 1 channel.
  • Checked just now. Nothing was sent because no channel is enabled.
  • A message naming the channels that failed and why.

Only updates you were not told about yet are sent. The button does not change the schedule. See How notifications work.

Note

Plugin and theme data can be a few hours old when you click the button. See Why is the update data hours old? for why, and how to refresh it first.

docs.title: Each update is reported once
docs.text:
On every check the plugin asks WordPress which updates are waiting. It then sends each enabled channel only what that channel has not been told about yet.

  • The plugin remembers, for each channel, the version of each plugin, theme and WordPress it has reported. If the update is still waiting at the next check, nothing is sent.
  • A newer version is a new update. If a plugin goes from 2.0 to 2.1 and then 2.2 is released before you update, you are told about 2.2 as well.
  • Once an update is no longer waiting, for example because you installed it, the plugin forgets it.
  • Each channel keeps its own record. Adding a channel does not cause the others to send again.

A check sends one message to each channel, listing everything that is new to that channel. It does not send one message per update. If nothing is new, nothing is sent.

Updates that a channel does not receive because of its routing are not reported to it, and they do not count as sent.

docs.title: Reminders
docs.text:
A channel can repeat the updates you have not installed yet. Set Reminders to Daily or Weekly in the channel's routing. The default is Never.

  • The reminder is one message listing all updates still waiting for that channel, not only the ones that were reported before. It is marked as a reminder (see below).
  • New updates are not held back. They are sent at once, as a normal message.
  • If a new update is found in the same check as a reminder that is due, you get one message: the reminder, with the new update in it. You never get two.
  • The first reminder comes one interval after something starts waiting for the channel. When nothing is waiting, the interval is cleared. The next update to wait starts it again.
  • A failed reminder does not restart the interval. The channel tries again at the next check.
  • A channel that is switched off, or is waiting because of Retry-After, gets no reminder. If you added or switched on a channel and chose not to send what was already waiting, that check sends no reminder, but the interval starts, so you are reminded about those updates later.

Reminders are decided at each check, so they can not come more often than the frequency to check. A reminder may go out up to half a check interval early, but never more than half its own interval early. This is because WP-Cron often runs a little late, and a strict rule would then skip a whole cycle. For example:

  • A daily check and daily reminders: each daily check sends a reminder.
  • Hourly checks and daily reminders: a reminder goes about a day after the last one, up to half an hour early.
  • Weekly checks and daily reminders: a reminder goes on every check.

Check for updates and notify now, and sc_wpun_run_check, work out reminders too.

docs.title: What a message contains
docs.text:
An email says:

  • A first line, "There are updates available for" followed by your site name and its address.
  • A line for each update: name from version X to Y, for example "WooCommerce from version 9.3.1 to 9.4.0".
  • Under a plugin: links to its page on WordPress.org and its changelog, when it comes from WordPress.org, or its own link if it has one. Under a theme: its link, if it has one.
  • Under a plugin: whether its author has tested it with your version of WordPress. The message also warns you if the new version needs a newer PHP or WordPress than your site has.
  • The address of your site's Dashboard → Updates screen, with a request to visit it to update. In HTML format this is a link, "Go to the Updates screen to update."

The subject is "WP Updates Notifier: updates available for" followed by your site name, with the channel's subject prefix first if it has one.

A reminder has the same contents, but its first line is "Reminder: these updates are still waiting for" followed by your site name and its address, and its subject is "WP Updates Notifier: reminder of updates waiting for" followed by your site name.

The site address in the message is your site's home address, the Site Address (URL) under Settings → General. If it is wrong, see Why does a message show the wrong address?.

docs.title: When a send fails
docs.text:
If a channel fails, for example because the mail server refused the message, the plugin does not record those updates as reported to that channel:

  • The other channels are not affected. A failure in one never stops the rest.
  • The channel tries the same updates again at the next check.
  • The reason is shown under Last delivery on the Channels tab, and in the notice after Check for updates and notify now.

Some channels, usually ones from add-ons that talk to an online service, can be told by the service to wait before trying again. This is the HTTP Retry-After header. The plugin then leaves that channel alone until the time is up, at most seven days, and Last delivery says Rate limited, next try after and the time. Other channels carry on. When the wait is over, the channel is sent everything that is new to it at the next check. The built-in email channel does not do this.

A test message ignores the wait.

docs.title: Overlapping checks
docs.text: The plugin does not lock checks against each other. If you click Check for updates and notify now, or something fires sc_wpun_run_check, while a scheduled check is running, both can send the same update before either records it. You then get the same notification twice. This is rare and harmless for update notices, so the plugin accepts it rather than adding a lock.

docs.title: Where the checks come from
docs.text:
• The schedule. WP-Cron runs the check at the frequency you chose. See Settings.
  • The button. Check for updates and notify now runs the same check straight away and does not change the schedule.
  • Your own trigger. A system cron can start the check. See How do I run the check from a system cron?.

All three send only what is new.

For the list of hooks that let developers change this, see the hook reference.

docs.title: Settings in code
docs.text:
You can set any of the plugin's settings, and the options of any channel, from outside the database. This is useful when you look after several sites and want the same setup on all of them, or when you want to keep an address or a key out of the database.

A value set this way is read-only on the settings screen. The field is greyed out and says "Set by" and where the value comes from, for example "Set by constant SC_WPUN_SETTING_FREQUENCY". Saving the form never changes it.

docs.title: Where values can come from
docs.text:
For each value the plugin looks in this order and uses the first it finds:

  1. Constants defined in wp-config.php. These are always read.
  2. Environment variables, only if you switch them on (see below).
  3. The database, which is what you save on the settings screen.

Constants must be defined in wp-config.php above the line that says "That's all, stop editing!".

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Names start with SC_WPUN_SETTING_:

Constant Values Setting SC_WPUN_SETTING_FREQUENCY hourly, twicedaily, daily or weekly Frequency to check SC_WPUN_SETTING_NOTIFY_CORE none, all or major Notify about WordPress updates? SC_WPUN_SETTING_NOTIFY_PLUGINS none, all or active Notify about plugin updates? SC_WPUN_SETTING_NOTIFY_THEMES none, all or active Notify about theme updates? SC_WPUN_SETTING_HIDE_UPDATES true or false Update notice 
define( 'SC_WPUN_SETTING_FREQUENCY', 'daily' );
define( 'SC_WPUN_SETTING_NOTIFY_PLUGINS', 'active' );

A yes or no value accepts 1, true, yes and on, or 0, false, no and off.

docs.title: Hide the About tab
docs.text:
The About tab can be hidden, and only in code. Set SC_WPUN_SETTING_SHOW_ABOUT to false:

define( 'SC_WPUN_SETTING_SHOW_ABOUT', false );

docs.title: Channel options
docs.text:
Names start with SC_WPUN_CHANNEL_, then the channel's id in capitals, two underscores, and the option:

SC_WPUN_CHANNEL_<ID>__<OPTION>

The id is shown on the channel's edit form, together with the start of its constant names. The channel that a new install creates has the id email:

Constant Option SC_WPUN_CHANNEL_EMAIL__ENABLED Enabled (yes or no) SC_WPUN_CHANNEL_EMAIL__TO Send to SC_WPUN_CHANNEL_EMAIL__FROM From address SC_WPUN_CHANNEL_EMAIL__REPLY_TO Reply-To address SC_WPUN_CHANNEL_EMAIL__FORMAT Format: text or html SC_WPUN_CHANNEL_EMAIL__SUBJECT_PREFIX Subject prefix 
define( 'SC_WPUN_CHANNEL_EMAIL__TO', 'ops@example.org,me@example.org' );
define( 'SC_WPUN_CHANNEL_EMAIL__FORMAT', 'html' );

Add-ons that bring their own channels get constants named the same way. Their documentation says which options are worth setting.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Environment variables use the same names as the constants. They are ignored unless the environment variable SC_WPUN_LOAD_FROM_ENV is set to 1, true, yes or on. This stops variables that your host happens to set from changing the plugin.

SC_WPUN_LOAD_FROM_ENV has to be an environment variable. Defining it as a constant in wp-config.php does nothing. If a constant and an environment variable both supply a value, the constant wins.

docs.title: Whole channels in code
docs.text:
The SC_WPUN_CHANNELS constant defines channels as a JSON list. Each channel has an id and a type, and can have a label, enabled (on unless you say otherwise), settings and routing:

define(
    'SC_WPUN_CHANNELS',
    '[{"id":"ops_email","type":"email","label":"Operations","settings":{"to":"ops@example.org"}}]'
);

routing holds the same choices as the channel form: types, scope, core and remind. For example, "routing":{"remind":"weekly"} sends a weekly reminder of updates still waiting. remind is never (the default), daily or weekly. See Reminders.

These channels show Defined in code on the Channels tab. You can send a test through them but not edit, duplicate, disable or delete them there. A channel in code replaces a saved one with the same id.

docs.title: If a value is not valid
docs.text:
A value the plugin can not use is not applied:

  • An invalid setting falls back to the value you saved.
  • A channel with an invalid value does not send until you fix it.

The plugin tells you in two places: an error notice at the top of Settings → Updates Notifier, and a WP Updates Notifier cannot use some configuration values item in Tools → Site Health. Both name the constant or variable and where it was read from, never its value.

docs.title: More detail
docs.text: How the sources are asked, the field types, and how to write a source that reads from a secrets service are in Configuration sources in the developer guide.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
The General tab of Settings → Updates Notifier holds the settings that apply to the whole site. Where each update goes is set per channel, on the Channels tab.

Click Save settings after you change anything.

docs.title: Status
docs.text:
• Last checked: when the plugin last ran a check, in your site's time zone, or "never".
  • Next check: when the next scheduled check is due. If it says "not scheduled", save the settings to schedule it.

Running Check for updates and notify now updates Last checked but does not move Next check.

docs.title: Frequency to check
docs.text:
How often the plugin looks for updates:

  • Once Hourly (the default)
  • Twice Daily
  • Once Daily
  • Once Weekly

Shorter intervals are not offered, because each check also asks WordPress to refresh its update data from api.wordpress.org.

The schedule is run by WP-Cron, so a check only starts when someone visits the site, unless you run a system cron. See Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Notify about WordPress updates?
docs.text:
• No: WordPress updates are not reported.
  • Yes (the default): every WordPress update is reported.
  • Yes, but only major releases: only updates that change the first two numbers of the version are reported. 6.7.1 to 6.8 counts, and 6.7 to 6.7.1 does not.

docs.title: Notify about plugin updates? and Notify about theme updates?
docs.text:
Each has the same three choices:

  • No: not reported.
  • Yes (the default): every update is reported, whether or not the plugin or theme is active.
  • Yes, but only active plugins or Yes, but only active themes: only the ones in use.

On a single site, "active" means:

  • Plugins: plugins that are activated on the Plugins screen.
  • Themes: the theme you have activated and, if it is a child theme, its parent theme.

These settings are the first filter. A channel can narrow them further with its own routing, but it can not report what is switched off here. See Choose what each channel receives.

docs.title: Update notice
docs.text:
Hide the WordPress update notice from users who cannot update WordPress. This is on by default.

It removes WordPress's "a new version is available" banner from the admin screens of users who lack the update_core capability, such as editors and authors. They can not act on it. Users who can update WordPress still see WordPress's own notice.

This setting does not affect your notifications.

docs.title: Settings you set in code
docs.text: A setting supplied by wp-config.php or an environment variable is read-only here and says "Set by" and where the value comes from. See Settings in code.

docs.title: Why did I not get an email about an update?
docs.text:
Check these in turn:

  1. Was it already reported? Each channel is told about each version once. See How notifications work.
  2. Is the channel on? On the Channels tab, Enabled must say On.
  3. Does a setting leave it out? On the General tab, the setting for that kind of update must not be No, and if it is limited to active plugins or themes, the plugin or theme must be active. Check the channel's Routing column too.
  4. Did the send fail? Last delivery shows Failed and the reason.
  5. Has the check run? Last checked on the General tab says when. If it is old, see the next entry.
  6. Is the data old? See Why is the update data hours old?.

docs.title: Why did no reminder arrive?
docs.text:
Reminders are optional and per channel. Check these in turn:

  1. Is it on? Edit the channel. Reminders must be Daily or Weekly, not Never.
  2. Is anything waiting? A channel is reminded only about updates it receives that are still waiting. Check the channel's Routing column, and the General tab settings. If routing leaves nothing for the channel, there is nothing to remind it about.
  3. Has the first interval passed? The first reminder comes one interval after an update starts waiting for the channel, not at once. A new update is sent at once as a normal message.
  4. How often do you check? Reminders are decided at each check, so a weekly check can not remind you daily. See Reminders.
  5. Is the channel switched on and free to send? A channel that is switched off, or was told by a service to wait (Rate limited, next try after under Last delivery), gets no reminder until it is on and the wait is over.
  6. Did the last send fail? Last delivery shows the reason. A failed reminder is tried again at the next check.

docs.title: Emails only arrive after someone visits the site
docs.text:
The schedule is run by WP-Cron. WP-Cron is not a real clock. WordPress only looks for due tasks when a page is requested, so on a site that few people visit, a check due at 03:00 can wait until someone arrives at 09:00. A forum user put it as "I only receive emails after someone has logged in".

To fix it, run WP-Cron from the server's own clock. See How do I run the check from a system cron?.

docs.title: How do I run the check from a system cron?
docs.text: There are two ways. Use the first unless you have a reason not to.

docs.title: Request wp-cron.php
docs.text:
Stop WordPress starting WP-Cron on page loads by adding this to wp-config.php:

define( 'DISABLE_WP_CRON', true );

Then have the server request wp-cron.php on a regular schedule, for example every 15 minutes:

*/15 * * * * curl -fsS https://example.com/wp-cron.php > /dev/null

WP-Cron then runs the plugin's check at the Frequency to check you chose, and WordPress's own update tasks too.

docs.title: Fire the check yourself
docs.text:
The plugin's check can also be started from code with the sc_wpun_run_check action. For example, with WP-CLI:

*/30 * * * * cd /path/to/site && wp eval "do_action( 'sc_wpun_run_check' );"

This runs the same check as the schedule, and anything already reported is not sent again. It does not move the WP-Cron schedule, so Next check on the General tab does not change. If you rely on this alone, the time of your cron entry is the schedule.

Things to know:

  • The plugin does not lock checks against each other. If this overlaps another run, the same update can be sent twice. This is a known trade-off, and rare. See How notifications work.
  • A check started this way is not a WP-Cron run, so WordPress lets plugin and theme data get up to 12 hours old before it refreshes it. A check started by wp-cron.php allows 2 hours. See Why is the update data hours old?.

docs.title: Why is the update data hours old?
docs.text:
On every check the plugin asks WordPress to refresh what it knows about updates. WordPress asks api.wordpress.org, but it does not do so every time. It skips the request when it has asked recently:

How the check started Core updates Plugins and themes The schedule, or wp-cron.php 1 minute 2 hours Check for updates and notify now, or wp eval 1 minute 12 hours

So a scheduled check can see plugin and theme data up to two hours old, and a manual check up to twelve. WordPress also asks again early if the plugins or themes you have installed, or their versions, have changed.

To get current data before a manual check, open Dashboard → Updates in WordPress first. That page refreshes the data if it is more than a minute old.

Note

These limits belong to WordPress, not to this plugin. They keep your site from calling api.wordpress.org too often.

docs.title: Why does the email not arrive?
docs.text:
Send test on the Channels tab says "Test message sent" when WordPress has handed the email to your mail system. That does not mean the message was delivered. Check the spam folder first, then look at how your site sends mail.

  • The From address. With From address empty, the email uses the WordPress default, which is wordpress@ followed by your site's domain. If you set one, it must be at a domain your server is allowed to send mail for. Mail that claims to come from a domain the server has no permission for is often rejected or sent to spam.
  • SPF, DKIM and DMARC. These DNS records tell mail providers which servers may send for your domain. If your domain publishes a strict DMARC policy and the From address does not line up with the server that sends, providers can reject the message. Ask your host or mail provider for the right records.
  • The server's mail. Many hosts block or throttle the basic mail function WordPress uses. Install an SMTP plugin, or a plugin for a mail service, so WordPress sends through an authenticated mail server. Then send a test again.
  • Upgraded from 1.x? Versions before 2.0.0 sent from the administration email address unless you set another. If your From address was that same address, the upgrade cleared it, so mail goes from the WordPress default. Set From address if your mail setup needs one.

If WordPress itself fails to send, the reason appears in the notice after the test and under Last delivery.

docs.title: Why does a message show the wrong address?
docs.text:
The address in a message is your site's home address, the Site Address (URL) in Settings → General. The link to the Dashboard → Updates screen is built from the WordPress Address (URL).

Both can be wrong if wp-config.php sets WP_HOME or WP_SITEURL from the request, for example from $_SERVER['HTTP_HOST']. The check then runs in a request from a system cron or a visitor, and the address follows whichever host that request used. Set WP_HOME and WP_SITEURL to fixed addresses, or remove them and use the settings in Settings → General.

docs.title: I see a "configuration" notice or a Site Health item
docs.text:
An error notice at the top of Settings → Updates Notifier says "Some configuration values supplied from outside the database are not valid." The same problem appears in Tools → Site Health as "WP Updates Notifier cannot use some configuration values".

A constant, environment variable or other source gave the plugin a value it can not use. The notice names the constant or variable and where it was read from, never the value. An invalid setting falls back to the value you saved, and a channel with an invalid value does not send until you fix it. Correct the value, or remove it. See Settings in code.

docs.title: Why did Slack notifications stop?
docs.text: WP Updates Notifier 2.0.0 does not send Slack notifications, and your Slack settings are kept. If a Slack channel was switched on, the plugin tells you once by email, shows a notice on its settings page that you can dismiss, and adds an item to Tools → Site Health. The notice and the item stay while a Slack channel is switched on.

docs.title: A channel shows as unavailable: "needs WP Updates Notifier API …"
docs.text:
The add-on that provides that channel needs a newer version of WP Updates Notifier than this site has, so the plugin refused to load it. Nothing is sent through the channel, but its settings are kept.

Update WP Updates Notifier (or install an older version of the add-on) and the channel works again with no reconfiguration. These places show which module is affected and the version it needs:

  • the Unavailable channels list on the Channels tab;
  • a notice at the top of Settings → Updates Notifier;
  • Tools → Site Health, as "Some WP Updates Notifier modules need a newer version";
  • under the add-on on the Plugins screen.

docs.title: Where are the hooks?
docs.text: If you write code, every action and filter is in the hook reference.
